title: Configuration binding (Bind, Get<T>, validation)
hook: Configuration binding maps JSON and environment variable keys onto C# objects automatically — Bind and Get<T> are the workhorses, and validation catches bad settings before your API accepts traffic.

blocks.text: Configuration binding uses reflection to populate object properties from IConfiguration key paths. configuration.GetSection("OrdersApi").Get<OrdersApiOptions>() creates and fills an instance. Bind(existingInstance) mutates an existing object. services.Configure<T>() uses binding internally. Validation runs via DataAnnotations on the options class, IValidateOptions<T> implementations, or AddOptions<T>().ValidateOnStart() (.NET 6+) to fail fast at startup when settings are invalid.

entries.plainDefinition: Creates a new instance of T and binds the current configuration section to it.
Populates an existing instance from configuration. Returns false if section is empty.
Interface for custom validation logic registered in DI. Runs when options are created.
entries.example: Validate(JwtOptions, name) => options.Issuer is null ? ValidateOptionsResult.Fail(...) : Success

entries.plainDefinition: Extension that validates options when the host starts, not on first injection.

blocks.text: A Web API that starts with a missing JWT issuer or negative timeout will fail mysteriously on the first authenticated request instead of at deploy time. Binding validation turns configuration errors into startup failures — Kubernetes readiness probe fails, rollback happens, no customer impact. Senior interviews focus on ValidateOnStart, IValidateOptions cross-field rules, and the difference between binding errors (wrong type) versus validation errors (business rules).

blocks.title: Fail fast at startup
blocks.body: Use ValidateDataAnnotations().ValidateOnStart() or IValidateOptions<T> so invalid config prevents the host from accepting traffic. Catch misconfigured K8s secrets in CI/CD, not in production 500s.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Resolve configuration section
items.body: GetSection("Jwt") returns a subtree. Keys like Jwt:Issuer map to Issuer property.

items.title: Bind properties
items.body: Binder matches keys case-insensitively. Supports arrays, dictionaries, nested objects, and enums.

items.title: ValidateOnStart triggers at host build
items.body: Host calls options validation before Kestrel listens — pod fails readiness immediately.

diagram.title: Configuration binding and validation flow
diagram.source:
flowchart TD
  JSON[appsettings.json section] --> SEC[IConfigurationSection]
  ENV[Env vars Jwt__Issuer] --> SEC
  SEC --> BIND[Binder Get or Bind]
  BIND --> POCO[Options POCO]
  POCO --> DA[DataAnnotations]
  POCO --> IV[IValidateOptions T]
  DA --> RESULT{Valid?}
  IV --> RESULT
  RESULT -->|No| FAIL[Startup exception\nValidateOnStart]
  RESULT -->|Yes| DI[IOptions injection]

snippet.label: Options class with DataAnnotations
snippet.explanation: DataAnnotations express validation rules declaratively. Property names match JSON keys. Messages appear in OptionsValidationException at startup.

snippet.label: ValidateOnStart registration (.NET 6+)
snippet.explanation: ValidateOnStart runs validation when the host builds — before app.Run(). Missing Jwt:Issuer in K8s causes immediate crash loop with clear OptionsValidationException message.

snippet.label: IValidateOptions for cross-field rules
snippet.explanation: IValidateOptions handles rules DataAnnotations cannot express — cross-property dependencies and environment-aware checks. Multiple validators can be registered.

snippet.label: Manual Bind and Get for one-off reads
snippet.explanation: Get<T> is convenient in tests and startup code. Bind returns false for missing sections — useful for explicit error handling. Prefer Configure<T> for DI-injected options.

blocks.title: Config validation in Node vs ASP.NET Core
Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: ValidateDataAnnotations without ValidateOnStart — validation only runs on first IOptions resolve, possibly after health checks pass. Non-nullable reference types without [Required] — binder sets null silently. Binding to mutable static fields. Complex types without parameterless constructor. Expecting binding to coerce invalid strings ("abc" to int throws or defaults depending on version — test it).

blocks.text: How to prove it in production: integration test with WebApplicationFactory that omits required config section — assert host fails to start with OptionsValidationException containing property name. In K8s, invalid config causes CrashLoopBackOff before readiness — check pod logs for validation message, not generic 500. OpenTelemetry: add startup span event when options validate. For binding validation in multi-tenant apps, IValidateOptions can read IHostEnvironment and reject tenant-specific misconfigurations. PostConfigure<T> runs after binding for computed defaults.

blocks.title: Validation approach tradeoffs
rows: Without it, first request may fail instead

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Saying validation is optional for internal APIs. Not knowing ValidateOnStart exists (.NET 6+). Confusing binding (type mapping) with validation (business rules). Claiming [Required] on string? without enabling nullable context does what you expect — know NRT interaction.

interviewTakeaways: Binding maps IConfiguration keys to POCO properties via Get<T>, Bind, or Configure<T>.
ValidateOnStart fails the host at startup when DataAnnotations or IValidateOptions<T> reject config.
Production tip: pair ValidateOnStart with K8s readiness — invalid Jwt:Issuer never serves traffic.
60s: Get<T> creates and binds. Configure for DI. DataAnnotations for simple rules. IValidateOptions for cross-field. ValidateOnStart fails fast before Kestrel listens.
Follow-up: what happens if validation runs only on first IOptions access without ValidateOnStart?
commonPitfalls: Saying 'binding validates automatically' gets you rejected — binding maps types; validation is separate and must be enabled.
ValidateDataAnnotations without ValidateOnStart — first request hits bad config, not deploy time.
Strong answer: 'Bind with Configure, ValidateDataAnnotations plus IValidateOptions for cross-field rules, ValidateOnStart so K8s catches bad secrets before users do.'
introducedIn: Configuration binder in ASP.NET Core 1.0; ValidateOnStart in .NET 6

jsTsCorrelations.concept: Joi or Zod schema validation at startup
jsTsCorrelations.note: Node apps manually validate config objects after loading env. ASP.NET Core integrates validation into the options pipeline with ValidateOnStart — no separate validateConfig() function needed.
NestJS can validate env with class-validator decorators — similar to DataAnnotations. ASP.NET adds IValidateOptions for imperative rules and ValidateOnStart for host-level fail-fast.
